row.acts.note: HUD banner alternated 'Your turn' / 'Pip's turn'; each player dropped one disc per turn.

row.perspective.note: 3D view from above/behind my pink character beside a big blue board on a plaza floor. The camera stayed in one spot instead of following me, and the board runs off the bottom-left of the screen.

row.players.note: Bots (Pip, Bo, Moss) took seats and played at the same board with me. I only tested bots, not a second human.

row.body.note: My pink bean character walks with WASD, and a ring marks the column I stand in. Walking off the board gave the hint 'Walk onto the board', and E there gave 'Stand on the board'.

row.drop.note: Discs landed in the lowest free cell. Refusals shown: 'Not your turn', 'That column is full', and 'Stand on the board'.

row.giant.note: The cells are about as wide as my character, so the board is big. I could only see part of it at once.

build.1.note: A round ended with 'Pip wins!', with a yellow-ringed highlight on a winning line. Pip's discs look like a diagonal, and the HUD gave Pip 1 point. I did not see a draw.

control.interact.note: E dropped a disc in my column on my turn. Off turn it showed a refusal toast.

loop.closes.note: Turns and the out-of-turn refusal worked, and the game ended with a winner card showing 'Play again' and 'Menu'. I did not click Play again, so a restart is unverified.

playtest.summary: Turns, dropping with E, refusals with reasons, a bot win with the line highlighted, and the results card with Play again all showed on screen. I never saw a draw, and I never clicked Play again, so a restart is unchecked. The fixed camera that doesn't follow my character is the main rough spot.

acts.why: The turn banner switches between 'Your turn' and 'Pip's turn', and each turn adds one disc to the board.

perspective.why: It is a 3D view from above and behind a character standing beside a big floor board, but the board is always cut off at the bottom-left, and the tester says the camera did not keep up with their character.

players.why: Only bots (Pip, Bo, Moss) were seen sharing the board, and no second human ever joined, so playing with friends is unseen; the lobby's 'Play with friends' button is only a label.

body.why: The player is a pink bean that walks around the plaza and onto the board, a ring marks the column it stands in, and 'E: drop in this column' appears there; bots also walk to their columns.

drop.why: Discs show up on the board after each drop, and the tester saw the refusals 'Not your turn', 'That column is full' and 'Stand on the board'; the 'Walk onto the board' hint is on screen, but I could not check the lowest-free-cell rule myself on a board that lies flat.

win.why: A round ended with 'Pip wins!', four blue discs in a diagonal ringed in yellow, and Pip's score went to 1; across and up wins and the draw were not seen.

giant.why: The board fills the town square, and each cell is about as wide as a character, so the discs are at body scale.

findings: The friends part of their idea is unproven: every game seen was one person against bots, and the lobby's default Play is 'You and 1 bot'.
You can never see the whole giant board at once because it always runs off the screen, so it is hard to spot lines of four forming.
The board lies flat on the floor, so 'slides to the lowest cell' has no gravity you can see, and it is hard to tell which end of a column is the bottom.
A draw on a full board and 'Play again' starting a new round were never seen.

delivery.summary: Giant Four has a 7×6 board laid flat in the plaza, big enough to walk on. On your turn, walk to a column and press E, and your disc slides to the lowest free cell. If the column is full, or it isn't your turn, the move is refused and you're told why. rules.js now checks for four discs of one colour in a line (across, up or diagonal) through the last disc dropped. When that happens the winning line lights up and the round ends with +1 to the winner; a full board is a draw. Bots walk to their column before they drop. The number in a line that wins is the rules.need setting (4). The quick verify passed 21 of 21 checks (the contact sheet was skipped). One problem I couldn't clean up: shell commands were blocked, so a stray scratch file, games/pa11-four/rules.js.new (it only contains "x"), is still in the folder and should be deleted.

honest: Delivered on the third attempt with every gate passed and every promise seen by the play-tester; nobody has played it, and this is not the creator's verdict.

The second reader, which saw only the prompt, the promises with the tester's log and the screenshots, did not agree that everything was kept: "with friends" cannot-tell (every game seen was one person against bots; the tester marked it seen with bots only, as on PA10), the view partly (the giant board always runs off the screen; the camera did not follow). The loop's own proof said delivered; the reader is advisory and its words are delivered beside it. This is the gap it exists to show.
Two human players were checked by gate E (measure 5), not by the tester or the reader.
No economy or backend was offered: the pitch round chose not to, and the words did not ask for one, so the new part steps did not run in this build (they run in the tests only).

Round 5 (the pitch, on the stronger model) took 19 minutes and $6.83: with no shell of its own it started general-purpose subagents (the Agent tool) that ran validation scripts for it. No round was meant to have subagents; fixed after this run (headless rounds deny Agent and Task).

The account hit its session limit during the play-test; the round waited 31.5 minutes for the reset and ran again (claude.mjs patient), as designed. The wait is not in the round's minutes; it is in the attempt's.
The build round left a scratch file (rules.js.new, holding "x") it could not delete with the commands it was allowed; verify still passed with it there.

Attempts 1 and 2 were stopped by me after the loop went back and forth on the ledger; their fixes are commits d4470bd and c9e1b6d. Their records are summarised here; the transcripts (7 MB, machine paths) stay outside the repository.
